title: Modification of extraction method for community DNA isolation from salt affected compact wasteland soil samples
author: Zaveri, Patel, et al.
materials: Proteinase K (1.5 ml) (Thermofisher, India) was added to samples prepared in step 1–2 and they were incubated at 37 °C for 1 h. The content was mixed intermittently for proper distribution during incubation. One molar Al(NH4)SO4 (∼3.5 to 5.0 ml) was added to the total volume of mixture to achieve the final concentration of 100 mM and tubes were incubated for 15 min at 30 ± 2 °C temperature. SDS was added (3 ml; 20%) and tubes were incubated at 65 °C for 1 h. Al(NH4)SO4 was added to mixture for removal of humic acid and salt interferences. No further increase in the DNA concentration was observed with prolonged incubation after 1 h thus, it was kept up to 1 h only. Samples were centrifuged at 7500 rpm for 10 min at 30 ± 2°C temperature and supernatant was collected (∼30 to 35 ml). Soil pellet was re-extracted again with 10 ml extraction buffer by resuspending soil pellet and step 3–6 as shown in Fig. 1 were repeated [5]. During second extraction, 1 ml SDS (20%) was added due to proportionate reduction in starting volume of extraction buffer.

steps.title: Prepare soil suspension
steps.instruction: Mix 15 g dry soil with 30 ml extraction buffer (100 mM Tris‑HCl, 100 mM Na‑EDTA, 1.5 M NaCl, pH 8.0) to a final volume of ~40–45 ml and vortex for 1 min.

steps.title: Cell lysis and first extraction
steps.instruction: Add 1.5 ml Proteinase K (ThermoFisher) and incubate at 37 °C for 1 h with intermittent mixing; add 1 M Al(NH₄)SO₄ (≈3.5–5.0 ml) to reach a final 100 mM concentration and incubate at 30 ± 2 °C for 15 min; add 3 ml 20 % SDS and incubate at 65 °C for 1 h; centrifuge at 7500 rpm for 10 min at 30 ± 2 °C and collect the supernatant (~30–35 ml); re‑extract the pellet with 10 ml extraction buffer and repeat the above lysis steps, adding 1 ml 20 % SDS in the second extraction.

substeps.instruction: Add Proteinase K (1.5 ml) and incubate 37 °C 1 h with intermittent mixing.
Add Al(NH₄)SO₄ (1 M, 3.5–5 ml) to reach 100 mM; incubate 30 °C 15 min.
Add SDS (3 ml, 20%); incubate 65 °C 1 h.
Centrifuge 7500 rpm 10 min at 30 °C; collect supernatant.
Re‑extract pellet with 10 ml buffer and repeat steps, adding 1 ml 20 % SDS.

steps.title: Remove proteins and humic acids
steps.instruction: Combine supernatants from both extractions (~40–45 ml), split into two 50 ml centrifuge tubes, add half‑volume 1.6 M NaCl (10–11.5 ml) and 1 M Al(NH₄)SO₄ (~3 ml) to obtain 100 mM Al(NH₄)SO₄, incubate at room temperature (30 ± 2 °C) for 1 h, centrifuge at 7500 rpm for 20 min, then add additional Al(NH₄)SO₄ to reach a final concentration of 200 mM.

substeps.instruction: Mix the two supernatants together.
Divide the mixture into two 50 ml tubes.
Add 1.6 M NaCl (half the tube volume, 10–11.5 ml).
Add 1 M Al(NH₄)SO₄ (~3 ml) to reach 100 mM.
Incubate 30 °C 1 h.
Centrifuge 7500 rpm 20 min.
Add more Al(NH₄)SO₄ to bring total to 200 mM.

steps.title: Potassium acetate precipitation
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 2 ml TE buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 1 mM EDTA), aliquot into four 2 ml tubes, add 7.5 M potassium acetate to a final 0.5 M concentration (~0.03 ml), keep on ice for 45 min, then centrifuge at 13 500 rpm for 30 min at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 2 ml TE buffer.
Divide into four 2 ml tubes.
Add potassium acetate (7.5 M) to reach 0.5 M (~0.03 ml).
Incubate on ice 45 min.
Centrifuge 13 500 rpm 30 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform extraction and precipitation
steps.instruction: Transfer the aqueous phase, add an equal volume of phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1), mix, then add 0.6 vol isopropanol (~0.6 ml); incubate at –20 °C for 45 min and centrifuge at 13 500 rpm for 30 min at 4 °C to pellet DNA.

substeps.instruction: Add equal volume of phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1).
Add isopropanol (0.6 vol, ~0.6 ml).
Incubate –20 °C 45 min.
Centrifuge 13 500 rpm 30 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Dry, resuspend and pool DNA
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the four DNA pellets at ~30 °C, resuspend each in 10 µl TE buffer, pool the resuspended DNA, and run agarose‑gel electrophoresis to assess quality.

description: Method described by [1] for community DNA isolation from various types of soil samples was modified for wasteland soil samples collected from coastal areas of Gujarat. Extremely low microbial population ( <101 cfu/g of soil) was detected and hence higher amount of sample was processed for microbial community DNA isolation. For preparation of the solutions and glassware used, sterile Deoxyribonuclease (DNase) and Ribonuclease (RNase) free water was used as and when required. Commercially available kit (bead beating) and enzymatic lysis methods tested without any modification could not yield any DNA from such type of soil sample. Community DNA isolation method involving use of hexadecyl-trimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) even could not successfully extract DNA from wasteland soil [2]. Bench modifications were performed only for enzymatic lysis method and are described in this paper. The flow chart of working protocol is described in Fig. 1.
